description: Seat 2 of the room-code match, driven by the Node WebSocket client. The spec has to prove that an action the Node player sends round-trips into the browser's DOM, so seat 2 needs one card it is certain to hold: #84 Going Long is tagged Quickdraw (SPEC §6.2: "Starts in your opening hand instead of a draw"), so it is in seat 2's opening hand for every seed. It is a Field Spell, which §10.8 makes public in the backrow ("traps show as unknown, Field Spells are public"), so the browser renders it by instance id under zone-opponent-backrow-1 - a face-down trap would not be visible and could not be asserted. Its base price is 2 ("2 embiggen 4"), which seat 2 can pay on its second turn (player-turn 4; §2.3), and the Node player sends embiggen:false so no play-time picker is involved (R81). Its only effect is Armor 2 on its own hero, so it cannot damage, heal or end the match. The other 19 cards are inert in hand for the same reasons as 06-room-a: no Cast-on-draw (#21, #27 excluded), no second Quickdraw, no hand trigger (#89 excluded).
